objective: Rework after the phase E review (TR-E-1 = SEC-E-1, major): a late but validly signed PAYMENT.AUTHORIZATION.CREATED must not move an operation backwards. Every webhook event now has a complete origin list; every other origin is stored flagged TRANSITION_NOT_ALLOWED and changes nothing.
context: Reset to pending after review rev-mv3xhtuz-017cfbef. Read .eccode/reviews/drafts/phase-e-1.json (TR-E-1) and phase-e-security-1.md (SEC-E-1). Root cause: PAYMENT.AUTHORIZATION.CREATED had no `from` list, so the only gate was the payment state table, which allows capture_pending -> authorized (for CAPTURE.DENIED) and unknown -> authorized; a late genuine event therefore rolled a pending capture back to authorized and the next reconciler tick compensated the purchase. completedWork: (1) src/services/webhooks.js: WEBHOOK_EVENTS now carries, per event, `from` (the COMPLETE list of statuses it may move) and `fromUnknown` (prev_status values of an unknown operation it may resolve forward; empty = left to the reconciler). applyEvent checks the origin list first (the ALREADY_IN_STATE shortcut is gone: an operation already at the target, past it or in a foreign state is flagged TRANSITION_NOT_ALLOWED and untouched), then the state table as a second gate. Lists checked against the spec (Interface Contracts > Webhooks, L420-L427; Void rule step 4; states.js): PAYMENT.AUTHORIZATION.CREATED from approved, authorization_pending (spec: pending -> authorized; approved is the same moment before the return handler recorded it), fromUnknown none (spec ARCH-22 lets the hook fire on whichever path observes the move; an unknown operation now gets it through the reconciler's read-before-resolve, as the coordinator ruled); PAYMENT.AUTHORIZATION.VOIDED from authorized, fromUnknown authorized (our own void, also one whose answer was lost); previously created and approved were admitted by the state table although no authorization exists there; PAYMENT.CAPTURE.COMPLETED from authorized, capture_pending, fromUnknown the same two (a real capture report); PAYMENT.CAPTURE.PENDING from authorized, fromUnknown authorized (a repeat on capture_pending is now flagged, not silently ignored); PAYMENT.CAPTURE.DENIED from capture_pending, fromUnknown capture_pending (it already had this list); PAYMENT.CAPTURE.REFUNDED from refund_pending, fromUnknown refund_pending (the table already only allowed that; now explicit); CHECKOUT.ORDER.APPROVED informational, never moves. (2) test/api/webhooks.test.js: mapping table grew from 21 to 42 rows (96 -> 117 tests): AUTHORIZATION.CREATED from capture_pending, unknown prev authorized, unknown prev capture_pending, unknown prev approved, unknown prev authorization_pending, authorized, captured, refunded, authorization_failed, voided; VOIDED from unknown prev authorized (applied), unknown prev approved, authorization_pending, created; COMPLETED from unknown prev capture_pending (applied), unknown prev refund_pending, authorization_pending; PENDING from unknown prev authorized (applied) and capture_pending (flagged); DENIED from unknown prev capture_pending (applied), unknown prev authorized, authorized (now flagged); REFUNDED from unknown prev refund_pending (applied), unknown prev captured, refund_requested. Existing expectations changed with the rule: authorized + CREATED and authorized + DENIED are flagged (were ignored ALREADY_IN_STATE), unknown(prev approved) + CREATED is flagged (was applied), the hook test that went through an unknown operation now goes through an approved one, and the 'second event' in the hook test is flagged. remainingIssues: Behaviour change to confirm in review: an event for an operation already in the target state is now flagged (TRANSITION_NOT_ALLOWED, flagged = 1) instead of ignored (ALREADY_IN_STATE), and an unknown operation is never resolved by AUTHORIZATION.CREATED (the reconciler resolves it by reading the provider). lessonDecisions.note: The lesson applies to a hook or guard that maps file writes to a project record or root in a repository with several records; this rework changes a webhook service and its API tests and designs no hook, guard or root discovery, so its 'Applies when' list does not hold. The guard accepted every nested edit to my two files.
